developments: Asian markets failed to build on Nvidia's results: the Nikkei slipped 0.3% and MSCI's Asia-Pacific index outside Japan fell for a fifth day, Reuters reported, after Nvidia's board said it would not reinstate Jensen Huang and hired a firm to find a new chief executive.
US spot bitcoin ETFs saw net outflows of about $240 million on Tuesday, $209.5 million of it from BlackRock's IBIT, according to Farside data as reported by MarsBit.
Bitcoin was steady overnight near $64,570 on Kraken, while Zcash rose to about $960 from about $935 at the evening edition.
briefing.changed: Little moved overnight. Bitcoin is flat on the evening edition, Nvidia's after-hours gain did not carry into Asia, and Tuesday's ETF figures returned to outflows after Monday's small inflow. Zcash is the one clear mover, up about 3%.
briefing.question: Does UK inflation at 07:00 and tonight's Fed minutes add to the rate-rise fears that have weighed on bitcoin, or give it room to recover?
briefing.watch: UK CPI for October at 07:00 UK, consensus 3.6%. Then FOMC minutes at 19:00 UK. The next 🔴 event is the Fed decision on Wednesday 9 December at 19:00 UK.

lead.headline: Bitcoin holds near $64,500 as Nvidia's beat fails to lift Asia
lead.standfirst: Asian shares turned lower after Nvidia's board ruled out Jensen Huang's return, while US bitcoin funds lost about $240 million on Tuesday.
body: Bitcoin traded near $64,570 on Kraken at 06:30 UK on Wednesday, almost unchanged from the previous evening, after a 24-hour range of about $63,270 to $65,380.

Asian markets reversed early gains. Japan's Nikkei fell 0.3% and MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan slipped 0.1%, a fifth straight fall, Reuters reported. S&P 500 futures were up 0.3%. Nvidia beat forecasts on Tuesday, but its board chair said on the results call that the board did not intend to reinstate Jensen Huang as chief executive and had hired Heidrick & Struggles to find a permanent replacement, Decrypt reported. The Wall Street Journal reported that the SEC is probing Nvidia; the SEC declined to comment, according to Reuters.

US spot bitcoin ETFs had net outflows of about $239.9 million on Tuesday, with $209.5 million leaving BlackRock's IBIT, according to Farside data cited by MarsBit. That followed a small inflow on Monday which had ended a run of outflows.

Rate expectations remain the backdrop. St Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem said on Tuesday the Fed may need several rate hikes and should act soon, Reuters reported. The US 10-year yield eased to 5.08%.
UK inflation figures for October are due at 07:00 UK, with economists expecting 3.6% against 3.5% in September. Minutes of the Fed's October meeting follow at 19:00 UK.

headline: Bitcoin was flat overnight near $64,570 as Asian shares slipped despite Nvidia's beat, and US bitcoin ETFs lost about $240 million on Tuesday. UK inflation at 07:00 and Fed minutes at 19:00 are today's tests.
spoken: Cryptonaire Post, morning edition. Bitcoin was steady overnight at about sixty four thousand five hundred dollars. Nvidia's strong results did not lift Asia: Japan's Nikkei slipped, after Nvidia's board ruled out Jensen Huang's return as chief executive. US bitcoin funds lost about two hundred and forty million dollars on Tuesday, mostly from BlackRock's fund. Zcash rose about three percent to around nine hundred and sixty dollars. Today, UK inflation at seven a.m., expected at three point six percent, and Fed minutes at seven p.m. Information only, not advice.

stories.title: Nvidia beat fails to lift Asia as board rules out Huang return
stories.why: The Nikkei fell 0.3% and MSCI's Asia-Pacific index outside Japan slipped 0.1% for a fifth daily fall, Reuters reported, while S&P 500 futures rose 0.3%. Nvidia's board chair said it would not reinstate Jensen Huang and hired Heidrick & Struggles to find a permanent chief executive, with Colette Kress staying as interim, Decrypt reported. The Wall Street Journal reported an SEC probe of Nvidia; the SEC declined to comment.
stories.caveat: Reports differ on Nvidia's after-hours move, from a gain of up to 3.8% to a small dip. Wednesday's US open at 14:30 UK is the real test.

note.read: The evening edition's relief from Nvidia's beat has faded; leadership and regulatory questions are now competing with the strong numbers, which leaves tech, and bitcoin with it, without a clear lift.
note.alt: Asia is simply cautious ahead of Anthropic's listing and the Fed minutes, and Nvidia could still rally at the US open.
note.change: Nvidia opening firmly higher at 14:30 UK with the Nasdaq following, or details of the SEC probe emerging.

stories.title: Bitcoin ETFs lose about $240 million on Tuesday, mostly from IBIT
stories.why: US spot bitcoin ETFs had net outflows of about $239.9 million on 17 November, led by BlackRock's IBIT at $209.5 million, with Grayscale's GBTC down $17.7 million, according to Farside data reported by MarsBit. Ether ETFs lost $29.1 million. Monday's small inflow, which ended a run of outflow days, was not followed through.
stories.caveat: Farside's own site could not be reached to confirm; figures come from a republished summary of its data.

note.read: Large holders in the biggest fund are still reducing exposure, so Monday's inflow looks like a pause rather than a turn.
note.alt: One day's IBIT redemption can reflect a single institution rebalancing rather than broad selling.
note.change: Two or three consecutive days of net inflows.

stories.title: UK inflation due at 07:00, expected to rise to 3.6%
stories.why: Economists expect October CPI at 3.6% against 3.5% in September, with core at 2.8% and services at 3.7% last month, AskTraders reported. The Bank of England raised Bank Rate to 4.00% on 5 November, so a hot reading would add to talk of another rise in December and move sterling against the dollar.

stories.title: Bitcoin flat overnight near $64,570 after breaking its 200-week average
stories.why: Bitcoin traded near $64,570 on Kraken at 06:30 UK, little changed from the evening edition, in a 24-hour range of about $63,270 to $65,380. CoinDesk noted last week's 12.6% fall closed below the 200-week average near $68,000; in the three earlier cases since 2013, bitcoin fell another 10% to 17% before recovering, which applied now would mean roughly $54,000 to $59,000.
stories.caveat: Three past cases are a tiny sample, and in 2022 the recovery was cut short by the FTX collapse.

stories.title: Fed's Musalem says several rate hikes may be needed
stories.why: St Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem said on Tuesday the Fed may need several rate hikes to control inflation and should act soon, Reuters reported. The dollar index held near 103.6 after its highest since April 2025, the US 10-year yield eased 2 basis points to 5.08% and Brent fell to $92.60. Tonight's minutes will show how widely that view is shared.

stories.title: Zcash up about 3% overnight to near $960
stories.why: ZEC traded near $960 on Kraken at 06:30 UK, up from about $935 at the evening edition, in a 24-hour range of about $907 to $973. Separately, Coinbase extended its USDC loans to New York, completing all 50 US states, though ZEC as collateral is not yet offered there, The Block reported.

stories.title: Anthropic set to price its IPO today
stories.why: Anthropic was due to price its shares on Wednesday ahead of trading, at a valuation of up to $1.4 trillion, with Bloomberg reporting guidance at the top of the range or above, Reuters said. A strong debut could steady tech sentiment; a weak one would add to AI worries.

stories.title: US judge acquits brothers in $25 million Ethereum bot case
stories.why: Judge Jessica Clarke in Manhattan acquitted Anton and James Peraire-Bueno of wire fraud and money laundering charges over a 2023 exploit that cost trading bots about $25 million, ruling prosecutors had not proved a material misrepresentation, CoinDesk and The Block reported. It was the first US criminal case over this kind of on-chain trading exploit.

explained.title: The 200-week moving average
body: The 200-week moving average is bitcoin's average closing price over roughly the last four years. Because it spans a whole halving cycle, many traders treat it as a long-term floor, and bitcoin has closed a week below it only a handful of times.

A break below it does not predict what comes next on its own. It tells you the price is below what the average buyer of the past four years paid, which is why it often coincides with heavy loss-taking.

investigating: Was Tuesday's IBIT outflow one large holder or broad selling? Farside's fund-by-fund data over the next few days and BlackRock's daily holdings would answer it.
What is the SEC examining at Nvidia? A company filing or a primary report beyond the Wall Street Journal's would confirm the scope.
